extracted.intended_audience: general internet users, publishers, educators, researchers, and potential commercial licensees interested in NewsGuard ratings and methodology
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural guidelines NewsGuard uses to assess, score, and publish ratings for news and information websites, including the nine journalistic criteria, scoring system, Nutrition Label content, and processes for review, updates, and publisher engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nine journalistic criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: NewsGuard assesses news and information sites based on nine journalistic criteria (described as "basic, apolitical criteria"), such as whether the site repeatedly publishes false content, whether it discloses who owns and finances it, and whether it corrects factual errors when they occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed definitions of each criterion are published publicly. Nutrition Labels consist of a grid showing the site's performance on each of the nine criteria and a written explanation of why the site received its score and rating. The site's trust score is determined solely based on these nine criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust score (0-100) and reliability rating
rubrics_metrics.description: Each site receives a trust score of 0-100 points which determines an overall rating ranging from "High Credibility" to "Proceed with Caution."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site's score is determined solely based on the nine criteria. The Nutrition Label and score together explain the site's overall reliability and any specific trust issues identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nutrition Label content and disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: A detailed "Nutrition Label" explains who is behind the site, why it received its score and rating, and specific examples of any trust issues the team found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nutrition Labels consist of a grid showing performance on each of the nine criteria and a written explanation. Each Nutrition Label contains the names of the writer and editors who worked on the rating. Nutrition Labels include evidence, analysis, and any comments provided by the site being rated; complaints from site proprietors are published and linked from the site's Nutrition Label.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trained journalist assessment and investigative reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: A trained journalist assesses the contents of the site against the nine journalistic criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysts are trained journalists who conduct reporting to determine relevant details of the website's ownership, financing, credibility, and transparency practices. The analyst drafts the written Nutrition Label based on that reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contacting websites for comment before publishing negative findings
rubrics_metrics.description: If an analyst believes a site may fail one or more of the nine criteria, the analyst will contact the website to attempt to seek comment before publishing the rating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a representative provides a comment, that comment is included in the written assessment of the site to provide the website's perspective. This contact allows the site a chance to remedy issues, point out missed information, or disagree—responses and complaints are published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial review and fact-checking of ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: The rating is reviewed and fact-checked by experienced editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple senior editors review every Nutrition Label prior to publication to ensure the rating is fair and accurate. The process includes review layers and fact-checking to mitigate individual bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic updates and re-reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: NewsGuard periodically updates its rating of each site; ratings are reviewed and refreshed at least annually as a matter of practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More frequent updates occur if circumstances warrant (e.g., change in ownership, change in practices, award, controversy). If a site changes its practices, its performance on criteria may change and the Nutrition Label will be updated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apolitical and equal application of criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The nine basic, apolitical journalistic criteria are applied fairly and accurately to all sites, regardless of topic, tone, or political leaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The same nine criteria are used for news-based and opinion-based sites and are applied equally to established newspapers, broadcasters, new digital websites, and popular bloggers. Multiple editors and fact-checkers review ratings to ensure fairness and consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rapid identification and assessment of trending or new domains
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysts monitor major news flashpoints and trending news to identify new or emerging sources of potentially false information and assess those sites quickly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For sites that frequently change domains or launch new domains with the same content, NewsGuard tracks new domains and applies its rating to that new website. The goal is to provide a NewsGuard score, rating, and Nutrition Label before a site goes viral when it is spreading potentially false information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and accountability in methodology and staffing
rubrics_metrics.description: NewsGuard practices accountability and shows its work by disclosing methodology, the names and backgrounds of analysts and editors, its investors, and publishing complaints and corrections when warranted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nutrition Labels provide evidence and analysis explaining judgments. The backgrounds of analysts and editors are linked from Nutrition Labels. Complaints from publishers are published on the site and linked from Nutrition Labels; NewsGuard will make public corrections when warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: No fees from publishers; conflict-of-interest safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: NewsGuard accepts no fees from the news websites it reviews and does not charge publishers to be rated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charging publishers would represent a significant conflict of interest and is forbidden by an ethics policy every editorial employee must sign. Revenue instead comes from licensing ratings and data to technology and other companies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-censorship approach to misinformation
rubrics_metrics.description: NewsGuard does not restrict or censor speech; instead it provides context to help users assess information sources rather than blocking or removing content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NewsGuard positions its approach as an alternative to blocking untrustworthy content or providing fact-checks only after false content has spread—offering context and ratings so users can decide for themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Browser extension permissions and user privacy practices
rubrics_metrics.description: The extension requests permission to read and modify web page contents so it can find links and insert NewsGuard icons; this is described as the only purpose for that permission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NewsGuard states it does not collect or store personally identifiable browsing history, servers do not store or transmit logs of traffic, and the domain lookup is only used to serve scores and Nutrition Labels. Learn more via their privacy policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial use restrictions and licensing for organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: NewsGuard's browser extension is strictly for personal use; any commercial use of NewsGuard requires a commercial license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial uses (e.g., content moderation, curating advertising campaigns) without a commercial license are prohibited by the Terms of Service. NewsGuard offers special licenses for researchers, nonprofits, academic institutions, and educational programs; companies can contact NewsGuard for data licensing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and selection of sites to rate
rubrics_metrics.description: NewsGuard rates more than 35,000 news sources responsible for approximately 95% of online engagement in the countries where it operates, deriving the list from data services that track online activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NewsGuard supplements data-driven lists with editorial judgment to include well-known influential sites not captured by engagement thresholds, accepts requests from smaller/new sites to be rated, and tracks and rates new domains launched with the same content.
